title: Adverse Weather Conditions
description: Extreme heat - hyperthermia, heat stroke, sun burn. Extreme cold - hypothermia, frostbite. Heavy rain - flooding, water pollution. Ice - slip trip fall. High winds - flying objects, building damage, affected working conditions. Electrical storms - lightening strike, electrocution. Fog - reduced visibility. Hail - vehicle/building damage, injury. UV Radiation - sunburn, cancer. Environmental damage
controlText: Monitor Weather Forecast. Emergency Response Plan. Extreme Heat: Regular hydration and breaks. Rotation of workers where appropriate. Use of cooling equipment. Ventilation. Use shade. Extreme Cold: Provision of appropriate PPE (jackets, gloves, coats etc). Regular breaks and rotation. Heating equipment. Reduce cold exposure as appropriate Heavy Rain: Use of waterproof PPE. Use of non-slip footwear. Postpone outdoor work as necessary. Cover Materials as appropriate. Do not walk in flood water. Move equipment and materials indoors and to higher ground as necessary. Ice: Analyse surface for ice conditions. Use appropriate PPE with appropriate grip. Postpone work. Use non-slip material. High Winds: Monitor wind speed. Avoid work at heights in high winds. Secure or Remove loose materials. Scrim removed/anchored on scaffolding or site fences. Housekeeping. Electrical Storms: Monitor lightning information. Postpone outdoor work. Work indoors where applicable. Avoid working near conductive materials. Fog: Appropriate lighting. Reduce speeds and increase spacing in vehicles. Postpone tasks that require clear visibility. Hail: Monitor weather reports. Cover Vehicles/Machinery/surfaces as appropriate. Work Indoors where appropriate. UV Radiation: Minimum 30spf sunscreen. Provision of appropriate sun protection PPE (sunglasses, long sleeve and long pants, hat). Install shade structures as required.

title: Asbestos Exposure
description: Impact upon health of personnel and surrounding public from exposure including: Asbestosis. Lung cancer. Mesothelioma. Pleural thickening. Pleural plaques. Respiratory and pulmonary conditions. Non-respiratory health risks. Environmental damage
controlText: Survey/Sample for asbestos before work starts on pre 2000 buildings. Avoid working with or near asbestos. Asbestos removal area is demarcated and Isolated where ACM removal is taking place according to ACOP. Controlled access to work area and signage in place. Employ licenced contractors to establish safe access where required. Ensure ongoing monitoring where exposure is present. Follow Asbestos Management Plan where applicable. Asbestos awareness training.

title: Chase cutter
description: Dust and particle matter. Electrical hazards. Noise exposure. Vibration hazards. Flying debris. Musculoskeletal strain. Cuts and abrasions. Fire hazard. Slips, trips, and falls. Equipment malfunction.
controlText: Training and competency. Safe work procedure. Use vacuum attachment or shadow vac to reduce dust. Select and use correct PPE - Gloves/Safety Glasses/Hearing protection/Dust Masks as required. Regular maintenance and inspection of equipment. Guards and handles are in place. Electrical Test and Tag in place and current. RCD in place as required. Take regular breaks to reduce stress. Correct use of blade. Restrict loose clothing. Hot Works Permit as required. Safety in design. Purchase cutter with all available safety features. Two hands on machine at all times.

title: Compressed Air
description: High pressure injuries - skin penetration, eye damage. Flying objects/debris. Noise. Hose whip. Respiratory hazards. Electrical Hazards. Oil mist inhalation. Organ Ruptures. Air Embolism. Equipment damage
controlText: Trained and competent operators. Correct use of PPE - Gloves/Hearing Protection/Safety Glasses/Dust Mask as appropriate. Regular equipment inspections and maintenance. Pressure relief valves. Pressure Guages accurate. Adequate ventilation. Secured hoses and connections. Safe work procedures. Emergency shut-off systems. Signage. Electrical Test and Tag. Oil-free compressors. Never Use to clean clothes or body.

title: Computer Workstations

Keep accessways clear. Correct Storage of office Materials. EAP as required. Wiring tied off and correctly covered where applicable.

title: Concrete Breaker
description: Untrained operator. Noise exposure. Vibration exposure. Musculoskeletal disorders. Flying debris. Falling debris. Electrical hazards. Dust/Silica. Fatigue. Slips, trips, and falls. Crush Injuries. Environmental. Equipment failure.
controlText: Training and competency. Safe work procedure. Select and use correct PPE (hearing protection, safety glasses and face sheilds, gloves, respirators as appropriate). Dust suppression methods as appropriate (water, shadow vac). Guards where appropriate. Exclusion zones as appropriate. Kickboards to prevent falling material. title: Concrete Works (inluding drilling, cutting and grinding)
description: Dust/Silica. Silicosis. Eye injury. Respiratory issues. Musculoskeletal disorders. Noise exposure. Cuts and abrasions. Falling objects. Flying objects. Crush injuries. Skin irritation. Environmental. Hand tools. Electrical equipment. Equipment failure
controlText: Dust extraction for tools. Wet down of dusty areas. Local extraction ventilation systems. Wet-cut attachments for saws. Pre-cut materials. Avoid sweeping dusty areas. Information, training, instruction, supervision. PPE - gloves, safety glasses, hearing, respiratory. Safe work procedures. Noise control. Equipment inspection and maintenance. Barriers in place as required. Battery operated tools where applicable.

title: Confined space entry
description: Oxygen deficiency. Toxic atmospheres. Flammable or Explosive atmospheres. Limited access and egress. Engulfment / entrapment hazards. Suffocation. Chemical inhalation. Intoxication. Poor ventilation. Communication challenges. Biological hazards. Psychological stress. Electrical hazards. Excessive noise. Poisoning. Drowning. Noxious Fumes.
controlText: Training and competentcy for working in confined spaces. Adequate ventilation. Atmosphere monitoring - DO NOT entere if LEL and/or UEL are outside of safe zone, or if Oxygen levels are outside safe zone (19.5% - 23.5%). Stand-by rescue person. Gas monitor on person. Gas monitor calibrated and in date. Risk assessment and planning. Shoring/Battering as applicable.  Confined space entry permit system. Emergency and rescue planning and training and equipment. PPE as appropriate such as Positive Pressure masks/Filters/Coveralls/Harnesses etc. Lockout / tagout procedures as applicable. Exclusion Zone. Safe entry and exit procedures. Signage and barrier controls. Adequate lighting. Medical fitness assessments. Regular inspections and maintenance.

title: Drills (including core)
description: Dust/Silica. Flying particles and debris. Vibration. Noise hazards. Electrical hazards. Ergonomic hazards. Slips. Trips, and falls. Live Services. Manual handling injuries. Cuts & Punture wounds. Entanglement. Hazardous Materials. Drill kick back. Environmental. Slurry. Equipment failure
controlText: Trained and competent to operaters. Safe work procedure. Correct selection and use of PPE (Hearing, Eyes, Respiratory / Gloves). Correct selection of tool for job. Environmental controls. Dust control measures. Slurry control as necessary. Cover and protect drains as necessary. Test and Tag of electrical equipment. Regular inspection and maintenance of equipment. Implement ergonomic practices. Safety features used on drills. Employment of safe work procedures. Manual handling controls. Risk assessments. Guards/Covers/Handles as applicable in place. Dont raise or lower drill by power cord. Battery powered tools as appropriate. Replace damaged drill bit. Dont use excessive force to drill into material. No loose hair or clothing around open geared drills. Identify live service locations. Isolate services as applicable. 2 hands on tool where applicable.

title: Drugs and Alcohol
description: Intoxication. Impaired judgement and decision making. Decreased motor skills and coordination. Reduced productivity and performance. Poor Quality of workmanship. controlText: Personnel education and induction. Clear drug and alcohol policy. Drug and alcohol testing. Employee assistance program (EAP). Supportive work environment. Report to manager if suspecting someone under the influence. Access to rehabilitation and recovery programs. Enforcement of policies. Monitoring and evaluation. Legal compliance. Inform supervisor/manager if taking prescribed medication. Do not operate equipment if taking prescribed medication that can impair judgement.

title: Dust/Silica
description: Respiratory problems - Silicosis/COPD/Asthma. Reduced visibility. Eye irritation. Skin problems. Toxic effects. Slippery surfaces. Environmental contamination.
controlText: Dust extraction systems. General ventilation. Use of correct PPE and respirator - fit tested where applicable. Dust suppression - Wetting down of surface areas - Wet cutting - on tool vacuums - shadow vac - hoses/misters. Air Monitoring as applicable. Signage and barriers. Housekeeping. Scrim on fences/scaffold. Shrink Wrap scaffolding. Drain protection in place to prevent slurry run off into drains. H-class vacuums as appropriate with silica. Bag and dispose of silica dust according to local regulations. Avoid sweeping dust. Exclusion zones and signage as appropriate around work area. Schedule time to conduct work where applicable. Health monitoring. Training on risk of dust and silica.

title: Electrical Equipment and Tools
description: Electrocution. Electrical Burns. Electrical Fire. Equipment blow out and failure. Poor maintenance. Slip trip fall. Untrained operators. Overloading. Arc Flash. Damaged tools and equipment. Live Services
controlText: Electrical test and tag of all electrical equipment. No leads in Water. Replace/Repair unsafe equipment. Tag out unsafe or expired electrical equipment - do not operate. Hang cords up out of way to eliminate trip hazards. RCD and/or lifeguard at electrical supply. Training and competency. Regular maintenance and inspection. Do not overload plugs with multi-boxes. Select correct tool for task. Avoid overloading circuits. Do not hold tool by lead. Substitute for battery operated tools where applicable. Safe Working Procedures/SOP. Identify live services as applicable. Isolate Power as applicable.

title: Environmental Damage
description: Air pollution. Water contamination. Soil contamination. Loss of biodiversity. Health risks from hazardous waste. Increased flooding and erosion. Noise pollution. Visual pollution. Extreme Temperature. Aquatic and Wildlife impact.
controlText: Substitute for Eco-friendly practices. Include environmental checks in regular audits. Spill kits and training. Drain protection. Correct storage for chemicals. Resource management. Environmental impact analysis. Waste reduction and recycling. Ecosystem restoration and conservation. Training and education. Community engagement and communication. Emergency response plans and drills. Use of environmentally friendly technology. Monitoring and reporting. Noise reducing practices. Dust controls. Environmental Policy. ISO 14001. Correct stockpiling of material as appropriate. Cover materials such as soil to prevent leeching.

title: Equipment Failure
description: Injuries to personnel. Electrical hazards. Fire and explosions. Chemical spills. Workplace disruptions. Increased workload and stress. Damage to other equipment or property.
controlText: Regular Inspections and service maintenance. Training and competency on equipment usage. Regular testing and tagging of equipment. Quality control. Emergency procedures. Use of correct PPE. Risk assessments.  Use of vendor and manufacture reference materials and support. Purchase of spare equipment. Equipment rental/hire accounts. Lock out tag out as necessary.

title: Falling Objects (DROPS)
description: Injuries and fatalities. Impalement and penetration injury. Crushing Injury. Cuts and abrasions. Damage to equipment and property.
controlText: Training and competency on effective controls. Effective communication with other workers in the area. Exclusion zones and signage. Use of spotter where required. Use of tethering system for tools and materials. Kick boards or other barriers. Housekeeping. Strop/tie downs. Scrim or shrink wrap scaffolding and edge protectoin as required. Crash boards where applicable. Downsize materials where appropriate. Engineering - Ute canopies or covers where appropriate. Keep tools stored in appropriate vassal when not in use (bucket, bag, toolbox)

title: Fall from Height
description: Serious Injuries and fatalities. Internal Organ damage. Broken Bones. Cuts and Abrasions.
controlText: Engineer - install handrails/midrails/barriers where there is a change of falling from one level to another. Training and Competency in Fall prevention. Eliminate need to work at heights where possible. Use of appropriate equipment correctly E.g. Scaffold, Swinging Stage, EWP, Platform Ladders. Heights and harness training as appropriate. Fall arrest or fall restraint systems as appropriate. Implement rescue plans as required. Conduct risk assessment. Use correct entry and egress routes. Monitor weather conditions. Heights gear and harnesses tested and tagged, and checked for faults daily before using. Housekeeping - accessways clear of material on scaffold. Kickboards/toeboards installed as appropriate. 3 points of contact as appropriate when accessing/egressing via ladders

title: Fire and Explosion
description: Burns/Injury to personnel. Multiple Fatality or Permanently Disabling injury. Smoke inhalation. Toxic gases. Environmental damage.  Catastrophic damage to building and surrounding properties.
controlText: Emergency response planning. Evacuation plans/drills. Suitable fire fighting equipment as required, tested and tagged as appropriate (extinguishers/hoses/sprinklers). Hot Works Permits. Move all identified flammable/combustible material away from Hot Works Area. Cover material with fire blankets or shields if cannot be moved from work area. Accessways and exits kept clear. Never leave flame or heat unattended. Correct storage of flamabble/combustible materials and/or chemicals. Substitute different tools that do not generate flame where applicable. 60 Minute minimum fire watch. Trained fire wardens. Fire extinguisher training US03271 as required. First aid with burns kit available. If cutting, direct sparks away from combustible material. Hot works policy.

title: Flammable rags
description: Fire hazard. Chemical exposure. Environmental contamination.
controlText: Safe work procedure. PPE - gloves, respirator as appropriate. Hang up rags out of direct sunlight to dry. Correct handling, transport, storage and use of chemicals. Correct storage of used rags to prevent ignition (covered in metal container filled with water and flame retardant). Correct disposal is accordance with regulations. Fire safety measures.

title: Forklift
description: Serious Injury. Fatality. Equipment damage. Tip-overs. Struck by hazards. Falling items/loads. Crushing hazards. Impalement. Emissions and ventilation. Falls from forklift. Noise pollution. Electrical hazards. Mechanical failures. Hazardous materials handling. Structural damage. Blind spots.
controlText: Trained and competent operators (F-Endorsement where applicable). Traffic management. Exclusion zones. Equipment maintenance and inspection. Safe work procedure. PPE. Communication system. Ergonomic considerations.  Spotters as appropriate. Do not lift above lifting capacity of machine. Do not lift persons on forks. Appropriate sized forklift for lift. Operate at safe speeds of 5km. Operate on flat ground. Appropriate wheels/tread. Wear seatbelt. Beacons/lights/indicators operational. ROPs FOPs TOPs installed. Lift items with appropriate lifting aids/trays/pallets that are fit for purpose. Wrap/Strap/Secure items on pallets/trays as appropriate. Be aware of surroundings at all times. Marked pedestrian walkways as appropriate. Travel with forks down low. Sound horn when reversing. WOF and Rego if applicable.

title: Gas Bottles
description: Gas leakage and toxic fumes. Burns. Fire and explosion. Asphyxiation. Ergonomic considerations. Corrosion and aging of container. Inadequate labelling. Improper storage. Improper transportation. Inadequate training. Hazardous substance
controlText: Safe Work Procedures. Clear labelling. Correct storage of bottles in storage container with ventilation per SDS. Correct and secure transportation of bottles on trolleys with chains where applicable. Regular testing and register of bottles. Leak detection and prevention. Fire presentation and control. Emergency response planning. Risk assessment. Tools and guages fit correctly and fit for purpose. Valves fully closed when not in use.

title: Grinder / Disc Cutter use
description: Grinder wheel fracture. Flying debris. Fire and explosion. Electric shock. Noise exposure. Hand-arm vibration syndrome (HVAS).  Inhalation of fumes and dust/silica. Sparks and hot works. Improper tool use. Inadequate PPE. Lack of guarding. Cuts/Lacerations. Serious injury. Electric Shock. Kick-back injuries. Equipment failure
controlText: Training and competency. Correct PPE - safety glasses, gloves, dust masks, hearing protection as appropriate. Use of RCDs as appropriate. Tested and tagged if electrical grinder. Correct guards in place at all times. Regular inspection and maintenance. Use of dust control systems (on tool, shadow vac). Emergency response planning. Safe work procedures. Fully charged batteries as appropriate. Correct tool/blade for task. Use tool with two hands to avoid kick-back. Do not over-reach. Hot works permit and controls as appropriate. Ensure blade not spinning and remove power source when changing blade.

title: Handheld tools - (trowels, dog bars, hammers, chisels, scissors, crescents, screwdrivers, cutters, brushes/rollers, scrapers etc)
description: Hand injuries. Struck-by hazards. Overuse injuries. Noise. Pinch points. Vibration exposure. Crushing. Cuts/Lacerations. Dropped items from height.
controlText: Trained and competent. Correct use of PPE - gloves. Regular inspection and maintenance. Use of tool tethers. Safe work procedures. Hands away from pinch points. Regular breaks if using continuously. Replace as necessary. Safe Storage when not in use. Supervision as appropriate. Select correct tool for the task.

title: Hazardous Substances
description: Chemical toxicity exposure (skin, eyes, ingestion, absorption). Poisoning. Fire and explosion. Chemical reactivity. Corrosivity. Carcinogens. Mutagens and teratogens. Allergens and sensitizers. Asphyxiants. Radiation. Biological hazards. Transportation risks. Fumes Environmental hazards. Manual handling and storage. Contamination. Respiratory illness. Neurological effects. Skin and eye damage. Spill and leakage.
controlText: Trained and competent in the handling and storage of hazardous chemicals. Correct use of PPE. Understanding of SDS requirements. SDS available on site (printed and/or Donesafe). Risk assessment. Chemical management (Labelling, storage, segregation, register). Ventilation and containment per SDS and as appropriate. Emergency preparedness. Regulatory compliance. Regular monitoring. Regular Health Checks. Spill Kits in place. Bunding or secondary containment as required. Spill management and training. Safe Work Procedures with chemicals. Isolate area of exposure from other people and workers. Barriers and Signage. Only store the amounts required for the task as appropriate. Remove Ignition sources as appropriate.

title: Heat gun
description: Ignition of flammable substances or vapours. Burns. Fire/Explosion. Flashover. Toxic fumes. Electric shock. Skin irritation. Inhalation of dust and particles. Noise hazard. Heat gun overheating. Electrical Hazards. Equipment failure
controlText: Training and competence to safely operate heat gun. PPE as required for task - gloves, safety glasses, respirators. Safe work procedures. Regular inspection and maintenance of equipment. Safe Working Procedures. Fire safety measures. Electrical safety measures. Noise control. Emergency response planning. Monitoring and supervision. Implementation of fire watch practices for up to 1 hour following heat gun use as appropriate. Hot Works permits as required. Ventilation as required. Allow heat gun to stand and cool before storing.

title: Hot Works
description: Ignition of flammable substances or vapours. Burns. Fire/Explosion. Flashover. Toxic fumes. Smoke. Skin irritation. Noise hazard. Overheating. Health Hazards. Catastrophic Damage to building. Loss of life.
controlText: Hot Work Permits. Risk assessment. Tested and Tagged Fire extinguisher (min 4.5kg) available at the work site. Fire hose ready and available at the work site. Remove flammable/combustible material from Hot Works area where applicable including paper, wood, chemicals, dust/debris. Protect Material in Hot Work area that cant be removed with fire blanket or welding screen as appropriate. Minimum 60 Min fire watch in place as required. Fire watch during and after work. Min 10m exclusion zone around Hot Work area were practicable (15m on lower areas if Hot Works is being conducted overhead). Erect barriers and signage around Hot Work area. No unauthorised persons in work area. Permit Issuers/Receivers training as required. Hot Work equipment maintained, checked and in good repair. Emergency Response Plan in place.  Safe Work Procedures. Fire Extinguisher training as applicable. Fire Warden training as applicable. Ventilation in place as required. Fire resistant PPE as required - clothing, gloves, eye-protection, visors. Gas detectors as required. Remove glass from work area if practicable or Protect with overlapping sheets of non-combustible material. Never leave flame/heat unattended.

title: (Poor) House Keeping
description: Slips, trips, and falls. Fire hazards. Falling objects. Hazardous waste accumulation. Insect and pest infestations. Health and hygiene risks. Clutter and obstructions. Tool and equipment misplacement. Cuts/Lacerations. Chemical spills. Ergonomic issues. Security issues
controlText: Risk assessment. Hazard identification & reporting. Conduct of weekly Work Area Inspection checklists. Clean up as you go. Ongoing monitoring of site conditions and clean up. Wearing of correct PPE for conditions. Appropriate signage and exclusion barriers. Manage slippery surfaces appropriately. Implement appropriate waste management practices to reduce waste in the area. Bins provided. Proper waste management. Correct storage of materials and chemicals. Use of signage and barriers. Designated Storage areas. Clean up Spills immediately. Plan deliveries to minimise the amount of materials on site. Safety in design - ergonomics.

title: Ladders
description: Slips trip falls. Fall from Height. Falling Material. Serious injury. Fatality. Incorrectly positioned ladders. Over-reaching. Contact with live electrical services. Unsecured ladders. Structural failure of ladder.
controlText: Do the job from the ground where applicable. Substitute ladder for MEWP or Scaffold where applicable for more stable platform. Tie off ladder at top or foot of ladder at bottom where applicable. If ladder cannot be secured, have a second person provide footing by holding the ladder for added stability at the bottom. Ladder permits in place when required. Ladder angle 4m:1m. ACOP. Risk assessment. Checks and inspections that ladders are fit for purpose before use. Select correct size/type of ladder for task. Carry ladders horizontally, not vertically. Perform work off platform ladder, not straight ladder if required. Straight ladders only for access/egress where applicable. Use non-conductive ladders around electricity. 4m clear of powerlines. Do not exceed safe working load of ladder. Do not overreach. Carry tools on belt - do not place on steps or hang from rungs. Ladders to meet or exceed AS/NZS 1892 portable ladder standard. Clearly labelled and not covered in chemicals or other materials. Steps to face work activity. Avoid side on work where practicable (drilling through bricks or concrete). 3 Points of contact at all times - avoid holding items when climbing.

title: Lighting
description: Reduced visibility. Glare/reflections. Shadows. Poor Contrast. Flickering or Stroboscopic effects. Slips, trips, and falls. Collisions. Strain and discomfort. Security risks. Increase in machinery operation risks. Serious Injury. Electric Hazards. Eye strain. Headaches. Disorientation. Struck by injuries.
controlText: Avoid working in poor lite areas where practicable. Install appropriate lighting in areas of poor lighting. Ensure the light source does not cause other hazards E.g. power cords, glare, reflection. Use natural light where appropriate. Implement emergency lighting where appropriate. Hang electrical cords up where applicable. Test and tag of electrical lights before use where applicable. Issue head lamps and torches when appropriate. Check and replace bulbs if flickering or blown.

title: Live Services - Electricity, Water, Gas, Telecommunications, Drains/waterways.

controlText: Live Service identification and mark up as appropriate. Lockout/tagout tags and locks. Energy isolation procedures. Conduct regular inspections and audits. Inclusion of temporary removal procedures. Establish clear communication and coordination channels. Permit to work procedure as necessary. Confirmation of Disconnections/Isolations/Terminations in place. Pre-work site assessments. Look up and live. Dial before you dig. 4m away from overhead powerlines. No flames near gas/sewer lines. Exclusion zones with barriers and signage where applicable.

title: Leading Edges
description: Fall from height. Serious injury or death from fall. Suspension trauma. Unstable surfaces. Lack of guardrail and edge protection. Improper access and egress. Adverse Weather conditions. Falling objects. Equipment failure. Incorrect use of appropriate fall protection systems. Pendulum effects.
controlText: Safety in Design. Install guardrails along the leading edge. Barriers and signage around floor openings. Cover floor opening and bolt down cover where applicable. Install safety nets under working area to catch falling workers or objects. Fall arrest or fall restraint systems where applicable. Heights and harness training. Self retracting lifelines as appropriate. Anchor points installed a suitable distance from leading edge. Anchor points above person where applicable. Steel lifelines where appropriate to prevent cutting on leading edge. Training in leading edge work. Job planning. Regular inspection and test and tag of fall protection gear. Toeboards, netting, lanyards to prevent tools and materials from dropping. Hard hats with straps on when working at leading edges.

title: Lifting equipment and materials (with crane, hi-abs, etc)
description: Falling loads. Equipment failure. Crush and pinch points. Electrical hazards. Overturning or tipping loads. Struck-by hazards. Manual handling injuries. Slips, trips, and falls. Visibility issues. Communication challenges. Collision with objects and structures. Exposure to hazardous chemicals. Rollover of plant. Serious injury. Fatality. Adverse weather.
controlText: Trained and competent Dogman / Rigger / Operator. Regular maintenance and inspection of lifting equipment - certified where appropriate. Crane lift plan where appropriate. Safe load management. Use of taglines on all crane loads. Select appropriate PPE (gloves when handling taglines). Establish Drop Zones and Exclusion zones including signage and barriers. Check for live services above and below ground. Ensuring lifting equipment is on stable and level ground. Establish effective communication systems when lift in progress(radios, hand signals, alarms). Implement emergency response planning as appropriate. Correct handling and management of hazardous substances. Do not attempt to crane loads in extreme weather or wind. Monitor weather. Correct sized lifting equipment/crane for task. Do NOT walk under suspended loads. No unauthorised persons. Do not stand in pinch/crush points. Loads correclty slung. Adequate set down area as appropriate. Outriggers used. ACOP. Do not hoist beyond capacity of lifting equipment. Allow sufficient clearance between load and buildings. Spotters.

title: Manual Handling
description: Muscular strains and sprains. Cuts and abrasions. Fatigue. Crush Injuries. Repetitive motion injuries. Back strain. Slipped discs. Loss of balance. Obstructed vision. Pinch points. Crushing injuries. Overexertion. Heat stress. Falling objects. Inadequate shelving or storage space. Inadequate handling equipment. Lack of training and competence. Overreaching. controlText: Training and competency on manual handling hazards and risk mitigation. Engineering controls or lifting aids such as pallet jack, trolleys, winch, handles, ramps etc where applicable. Job rotation. Task redesign. Individual weight limit (E.g. 20kgs). Team lifting. Correct use of PPE. Correct technique - Bend at knees, not at back - Keep loads close to body - Stretch/Warm up - Turn whole body in direction you want to go - minimise lifting above shoulders. Conduct risk assessment. Implement ergonomic workplace design. ACOP. Risk assessment. Plan activity beforehand. Musculoskeletal checks. Housekeeping. Adequate lighting and visibility in place. Regular breaks. Correct sized tool for task. Rotation of workers and workers fit for task. Downsize/Split loads to more managaeable sizes. Appropriate footwear. Lay non slip surfaces or grit as appropriate. Clean up spills/water where applicable in traffic areas.

title: Mobile Elevating Work Platforms (MEWP)
description: Falls from height. Tip-over and collapses. Overhead services - Electrocution. Falling objects. Entrapment. Equipment malfunction. Adverse Weather conditions. Unlevel ground. Collision. Overreaching or overloading. Limited access. Serious Injury. Fatality. Public Safety. Struck by injuries. Pinch points. Overhead and Ground Obstacles. Poor Housekeeping. Unauthorised personnel. Damage to property
controlText: Trained and competent operator. Do not use in adverse weather, reschedule work as appropriate. Substitute EWP for Scaffold when practicable. Correct PPE. Regular equipment inspections (MEWP log book). Safe Work Plan and risk assessment. Safe work load limit adherence. Operate on stable level ground. Outriggers/Stabilisers used where applicable. Permit to Work for heights where appropriate. Heights trained operators in knuckle boom with tagged and tested harness/lanyards. title: Mobile Phones
description: Distractions from task and safety. Slower reaction times. Impaired judgement. Decreased awareness of surroundings. Poor vehicle control. Increased risk of accidents. Legal consequences. Increased insurance premiums. Reputational damage.
controlText: Implementation and use of hand-free/Bluetooth devices when driving. Promotion of safe driving practices. Technology solutions. Training and communications. title: Mobile Plant

Exhaust and emissions. Entanglement. Spills and leaks. Fire. Unauthorised operation. Equipment failure. Serious injury. Fatality. Serious Damage to buildings/structures.
controlText: Training and competence in operating relevant mobile plant. Traffic management. Exclusion zones or Plant operating zones as applicable. Regular service/maintenance and inspections of plant. Use of correct PPE. Clear safety signage. Speed controls/limits observed. Spill prevention and spill kits in place. Effective lighting. Vibration and noise control. Restricted access. Fire safety equipment. Authorised personnel only in working area. Eye or radio contact with operator before approaching. title: Noise

Erect signage warning of noise levels and PPE requirements. Distance workers from noisy work where appliable. Regular Health checks including hearing. Regular maintenance of equipment.

title: Other Contractors

Crossover of tasks and increased hazards. Unpredictable movements of personnel moving through work area. Serious injury or fatality. Poor communication. Quality defects. Safety Hazards.
